title: Charolais by Chef Austin Simmons™ Now Open at Hughes Landing®
body_text: Charolais by Chef Austin Simmons™ Now Open at Hughes Landing® Chef Austin Simmons returns to The Woodlands® with a new signature restaurant, reinforcing Howard Hughes Communities’ commitment to bringing standout culinary talent to the community THE WOODLANDS (July 14, 2026) — Howard Hughes Communities™ today announced the opening of Charolais by Chef Austin Simmons, a new restaurant at Hughes Landing that marks the return of one of The Woodlands’ most recognized culinary figures. For residents who came to know Simmons through his impact on the local dining scene, Charolais brings a highly anticipated new destination to the community he has helped shape. Known for his distinctive approach to hospitality and his deep focus on premium beef, Simmons has built a loyal following in The Woodlands and earned broader national attention for his steak program. At Charolais, he brings that same standard of craftsmanship to a concept centered on exceptional ingredients, interactive dining, and a guest experience designed to feel both elevated and welcoming. Located in Hughes Landing, Charolais adds a new draw for residents, visitors, and the area’s growing daytime population, while further strengthening the district’s position as a premier destination for dining, hospitality, and lifestyle experiences in The Woodlands. “Opening Charolais in The Woodlands means a great deal to me because this community has been such an important part of my story,” said Chef Austin Simmons. “We wanted to create a place that reflects the energy, pride, and standards of this market — a restaurant built around exceptional beef, thoughtful hospitality, and an experience people here can feel is truly their own.” Charolais introduces a modern dining experience where guests can customize steak boards by selecting specific cuts and preferred preparation methods, including live fire, cast iron, high-temperature broiling, and other modern cooking techniques. That experience is grounded in Chef Simmons’ Hoof to Plate™ philosophy, which emphasizes ingredient integrity, traceability, and quality from ranch to table. Through Chef & Rancher™, Chef Simmons’ venture with Texas rancher Larry Ludeke, the concept maintains oversight of the beef program from genetic selection and animal husbandry to processing and final cuts. “For a community like The Woodlands, local impact matters,” said Jim Carman, President of the Texas Region for Howard Hughes Communities. “Chef Austin Simmons is not just an acclaimed chef. He is a talent people here know and are excited to see return in a major way. Charolais brings a distinctive new experience to Hughes Landing and reflects our commitment to continuing to elevate the quality and character of The Woodlands.” Designed by gin design group and built by Texana Builders, the 200-seat restaurant features a main dining room with an open kitchen, a social bar with a chef-driven cocktail program and an open-air patio. Two private dining rooms accommodate 24 and 36 guests for corporate gatherings and special events, with the option to expand into the social bar or patio for larger groups. Adjacent to the restaurant, C&R Market extends the Charolais experience beyond the dining room, offering signature Chef & Rancher products for purchase, including premium cuts of beef from the same program featured on the menu, branded apparel, and other items to take home. The restaurant’s location in Hughes Landing, an amenity-rich district along Lake Woodlands, enhances walkable access for nearby businesses and residents, including those at The Ritz-Carlton Residences, The Woodlands, and 1 Riva Row. Surrounded by dining, retail, entertainment, and office destinations, Charolais contributes to the continued growth of The Woodlands Town Center as the area’s premier destination for lifestyle and business activity. C&R Market is open Tuesday through Thursday from noon to 9 p.m., Friday and Saturday from noon to 10 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 3 p.m. For more information, please visit www.chefrancher.com . Charolais is now open Tuesday through Thursday from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. and Friday and Saturday from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. For more information, visit www.chefaustincharolais.com or follow @charolaisbyaustinsimmons on Instagram. About Charolais by Chef Austin Simmons ™ Charolais is built around Chef Simmons’ Hoof to Plate™ philosophy, with Chef & Rancher overseeing the beef program from genetic selection and animal husbandry to processing and final cuts. That approach allows the concept to deliver exceptional beef with the traceability, consistency, and craftsmanship at the heart of the dining experience. Adjacent to the restaurant, C&R Market offers signature Chef & Rancher products for purchase, including premium cuts of beef from the same program featured on the menu, branded apparel, and other items to take home. Standard dining reservations can be made through Resy. For private dining inquiries and event bookings, visit Charolais . About The Woodlands® The Woodlands is a Howard Hughes community spanning 28,500 acres, located 27 miles north of downtown Houston. Home to nearly 125,000 residents and over 70,000 employees, The Woodlands combines award-winning residential neighborhoods with a thriving commercial core that includes Class A office towers, shopping, dining, hospitality, and world-class healthcare. With 36% of its land preserved as open green space, The Woodlands offers an exceptional balance of urban amenities and natural beauty and is pre-certified under the LEED for Cities and Communities program, reflecting its leadership in sustainable community development. Consistently ranked among the best places to live in America, The Woodlands is a model for sustainable growth and economic vitality. Learn more at TheWoodlands.com. About Howard Hughes Communities™ Howard Hughes Communities, the real estate platform of Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH), develops, owns, and operates the nation’s premier large-scale master planned communities and mixed-use developments. The company’s award-winning assets include The Woodlands®, Bridgeland®, and The Woodlands Hills® in Greater Houston; Summerlin® in Las Vegas; Teravalis™ in Greater Phoenix; Ward Village® in Honolulu; and Merriweather District in Columbia, Maryland. The Howard Hughes Communities portfolio is strategically positioned to meet and accelerate development based on market demand, resulting in one of the strongest real estate platforms in the country. Dedicated to innovative placemaking, the company is recognized for its ongoing commitment to design excellence and to the cultural life of its communities. For additional information, visit communities.howardhughes.com . Media Contact Howard Hughes Communities Katelyn Elliott, 205-470-3757 [email protected]

title: Apple reports third quarter results
summary: Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 third quarter ended June 27, 2026.
body_text: PRESS RELEASE July 30, 2026 Apple reports third quarter results June quarter records for total company revenue and EPS iPhone, Mac and Services revenue set new June quarter records CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 third quarter ended June 27, 2026. The Company posted quarterly revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16 percent year over year. Company gross margin was 50.1 percent, including a favorable impact of approximately 2 percentage points from tariff refunds. Diluted earnings per share was $2.02, up 29 percent year over year, and included a favorable impact of $0.11 from tariff refunds. “Today, Apple is proud to report our strongest June quarter ever, with double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services, and in every geographic segment,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. “At WWDC26, we were thrilled to introduce the all-new Siri AI, alongside all of Apple’s latest software innovations and important new child safety features.” “We are very pleased with our record business performance during the quarter, which set new June quarter records for both EPS and operating cash flow,” said Kevan Parekh, Apple’s CFO. “Our installed base of active devices also reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.” Apple’s board of directors has declared a cash dividend of $0.27 per share of the Company’s common stock. The dividend is payable on August 13, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on August 10, 2026. Apple will provide live streaming of its Q3 2026 financial results conference call beginning at 2:00 p.m. PT on July 30, 2026, at apple.com/investor/earnings-call . The webcast will be available for replay for approximately two weeks thereafter. title: Descartes XPS Ship Adds FedEx Extra Small Box Support for Ecommerce Sellers
summary: Descartes XPS Ship™ adds support for the FedEx Extra Small Box, giving ecommerce sellers another packaging option for compact domestic shipments.
body_text: Descartes XPS Ship™ now supports the FedEx® Extra Small Box, expanding packaging choices for ecommerce sellers shipping merchandise. The option is available for supported standard FedEx services and eligible FedEx One Rate® shipments. FedEx introduced the box in February 2026. It measures 7-1/4 by 2-1/2 by 4-11/16 inches and supports shipments up to 50 pounds, subject to FedEx service and packaging requirements. For expedited US shipments, One Rate pricing is based on the package type, delivery service, and destination. FedEx-provided packaging is required. For ecommerce sellers, the smaller format may reduce unused space and offer a lower flat-rate tier when products do not need a FedEx Small Box. Descartes estimates shippers could save at least $3 per package compared with that option, although results depend on the shipment, account, service, destination, and agreement. Sellers using their own FedEx accounts can select the Extra Small Box in Descartes XPS Ship for applicable shipments. Teams using FedEx Base Rates should first update or import the rate cards. Before adopting it broadly, compare costs by SKU, service, destination, packing protection, and negotiated rates. “We are thrilled that XPS Ship has released the FedEx One Rate Extra Small Box option on the platform. This additional option gives us a more competitive shipping rate, which in turn helps us keep costs low for our customers,” said Dylan Paulson, General Manager at eparts.shop . Book a Descartes demo to learn how XPS Ship can help you choose right-sized packaging, compare available FedEx services, and control shipping costs.

title: Call monitoring software: what it covers beyond recording
summary: Learn what call monitoring software actually does, why manual sampling leaves gaps, and how to evaluate a full-coverage platform.
body_text: See how full-coverage monitoring catches quality and compliance issues that live spot-checks miss. Your QA team can review perhaps 20 calls a week per agent, if they’re fast. Your contact center handles thousands. That gap is where compliance risk hides, where coaching opportunities go stale, and where a customer experience problem festers until it shows up in a customer satisfaction (CSAT) report or a regulator’s inquiry. Most teams still run QA manually: a supervisor picks a handful of calls, scores them against a rubric, and moves on. It’s slow, and it only ever touches a sliver of what actually happened on the phones. Call monitoring software changes that. It analyzes 100% of interactions instead of a sample, flags compliance issues automatically, surfaces coaching opportunities in real time, and separates platforms that just archive audio from ones that help you catch problems before they compound. Key takeaways Call monitoring software scores quality and compliance signals, not just archived audio. Manual review typically covers only a small percentage of your total calls. Full-coverage monitoring surfaces patterns sampled reviews structurally can’t catch. Evaluate platforms on coverage, workflow fit, and how actionable the output is. RingCX’s native AI Quality Management scores 100% of interactions automatically. What is call monitoring software? Call monitoring software evaluates live and recorded calls against defined quality and call center compliance criteria , then surfaces the results for coaching and audit purposes. It’s the analysis layer that sits on top of your calls, not just the storage layer underneath them. That distinction matters for how you budget and staff QA. A platform that only stores audio still requires a human to listen, score, and log every interaction you want reviewed. A platform built for conversation analytics does that scoring automatically at a scale no QA team could match manually. What call monitoring software actually does At its core, call monitoring software listens to, records, and then uses conversational intelligence to run every call against scoring criteria you define. Did the agent verify identity, disclose required terms, follow the escalation path, hit the tone and empathy markers you coach toward? Most of all, it does this across every interaction, not a sampled subset. Call monitoring software also flags compliance and procedural gaps automatically. If an agent skips a required disclosure or a call touches a regulated topic without the right script cues, the system catches it the moment the call ends, not weeks later during an audit. The output feeds coaching, not just record-keeping. Supervisors get real-time dashboards with key performance indicators (KPIs) and agent performance trends across teams. They can see who is slipping on a specific skill, which scripts underperform, or where compliance risk clusters. Metrics like average handling time, first-call resolution rate, and call duration become coaching inputs, not just historical logs. That’s fundamentally different from just maintaining a stack of individually scored transcripts. This also changes what a call center manager’s week looks like. Instead of spending most of their time listening to calls and filling out evaluation forms, they spend it reviewing trend reports and building coaching plans around what the data already flagged. The scoring work moves off their calendar, while the judgment work stays on it. Call monitoring versus call recording Recording captures the call. Monitoring evaluates it. Those are two different jobs, and a lot of platforms only do the first one well. A recording system gives you an audio file and maybe a transcript. That’s useful for dispute resolution and training reference, but it doesn’t tell you anything until someone listens to it. Monitoring software applies scoring criteria automatically, so you get a quality score, a compliance flag, or a coaching note without a human having to review the file first. If your current stack only records, you’re still doing QA manually. You’ve just made the manual step easier to schedule. Types of call monitoring software Call monitoring platforms generally fall into three categories. Knowing which one you’re evaluating matters more than any single feature checklist. Contact center QA solutions Native contact center QA tools live inside your existing contact center platform and score calls automatically as part of the same system that routes and records them. Because they’re built into the platform, they don’t require a separate login or data sync, and they typically cover 100% of interactions by default instead of as an add-on. Call recording tools Call recording platforms with analytics add-ons start as a recording and storage tool, then layer scoring or tagging features on top. These work well if you already have a recording system you like, but the analysis layer is often bolted on rather than native to the workflow, so coverage and integration depth vary widely from vendor to vendor. Conversation intelligence software Standalone conversation intelligence platforms sit outside any single contact center or phone system and connect to multiple communications tools at once. They’re built for organizations that want one quality and compliance standard across contact center, sales, and service teams, not a tool scoped to a single department. Why manual call monitoring leaves gaps Manual monitoring is expensive to scale, so most teams never scale it past a handful of reviewers. Live monitoring ties up a supervisor for the length of the call. Manual review after the fact ties up a supervisor’s time and delays coaching by days, often too late to matter. Neither approach covers enough ground. The result is most teams sample a small fraction of their calls and extrapolate from there. In an article covering AI in customer care, McKinsey found that manual QA is often limited to less than 5% of total call volume at most contact centers. Under 5% coverage means the other 95% of your calls go unreviewed. Outliers, edge cases, and slow-building compliance drift don’t show up in a sample that small. They show up later, in an audit finding, a regulatory complaint, or a CSAT dip your team can’t trace back to a root cause. A 5% sample and 100% coverage carry entirely different risk profiles. Think about how a sample gets picked in most centers: a supervisor grabs whatever calls are easiest to pull, often the ones flagged by a customer complaint or an obvious escalation. That approach already skews toward the calls most likely to look bad and away from the quiet, slow-building issue, like a script deviation an agent repeats 40 times before anyone notices. A 5% sample built that way tells you about your worst days, not your average ones. The business case for full-coverage monitoring Auditing your QA spend gets a lot more interesting once you look at what automated coverage actually returns. In the same article, McKinsey estimates that companies using AI to monitor customer interactions can see more than 50% savings in QA costs, up to 30% improvement in agent performance, and up to 10% improvement in CSAT. Run those numbers against your current QA headcount and review backlog. If you’re paying a team to manually score a 5% sample, automating that scoring frees those hours for the coaching conversations that actually move performance, not the data entry that precedes them. Full coverage also changes when problems surface. Instead of catching a compliance gap three months in during an audit, you catch it on day one because every call gets scored. Instead of coaching an agent on last week’s flagged call, you coach on this morning’s pattern across dozens of calls. That’s the real shift: coaching moves from reactive, built around whichever calls happened to get sampled, to pattern-based, built around what’s actually happening across the floor. What to look for when evaluating call monitoring software The right platform closes the gap between what happens on a call and what a supervisor can act on. Use these five criteria to separate tools that automate quality assurance from tools that just digitize it. 1. Coverage Ask any vendor directly whether the platform scores 100% of interactions or a sampled subset. A platform that still relies on sampling has only automated part of the old process, and the coverage gap remains. 2. Integration with your existing stack Check integration with the contact center and communications platform you already run. Look for systems that support smart call routing, interactive voice response (IVR) integration, and other core platform features. Monitoring software that lives outside your existing workflow adds a login, a data sync, and a gap between where calls happen and where they get scored. That is where adoption stalls. Workforce planning teams feel this friction directly when scheduling and coaching data live in separate systems. This is why it’s worth reviewing your workforce management approach alongside any QA platform decision. 3. Actionability A quality score with no context doesn’t help a supervisor coach anyone. Look for output that flags the specific moment in the call that triggered the score, ties it to a coachable skill, and tracks it over time. Raw numbers on a dashboard are a reporting exercise. Contextualized flags tied to specific coaching actions are a performance program. 4. Compliance posture Compliance posture describes how consistently a vendor’s platform, data handling, and internal controls meet the regulatory standards that apply to your industry, not whether the company can produce a certificate on request. A strong compliance posture pairs third-party audited certifications with controls that hold up under an actual audit or regulatory review, not just marketing copy. Ask any vendor for proof of relevant certifications and attestations before you sign, including: SOC 2 (Type 2): An independent audit validates security, availability, and confidentiality controls, typically renewed annually. ISO 27001: Certifies that the vendor’s information security management system meets international standards for confidentiality, integrity, and availability. HIPAA: Relevant if calls involve protected health information. Look for a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and controls mapped to HIPAA safeguards, not just a mention of the acronym. GDPR: Relevant if you handle EU resident data. Look for documented data processing agreements and data residency options, since GDPR compliance is a legal obligation, not a certification a vendor can simply hold. PCI DSS: Relevant if calls or recordings ever touch payment card data. RingCentral publishes its current compliance certifications , including ISO 27001, SOC 2+, and PCI attestations for its contact center platform, a useful benchmark for what documentation any vendor should be able to produce. Confirm the platform tracks adherence against your industry’s specific regulatory requirements, not a generic script-adherence check. Review this against your call center compliance requirements before you commit to a vendor. 5. Speed to flag Catch a compliance gap the same day, and you’ve fixed it. Catch the same gap in a quarterly audit, and you’ve got a finding, and possibly a report you have to file. Ask any vendor how long it takes between a call ending and a flagged issue reaching a supervisor’s queue. An answer of “during the next review cycle” means the coverage problem is still there, just running on a faster clock. How RingCX helps you monitor 100% of calls Contact center leaders don’t need a monitoring tool that depends on a supervisor catching the right call live. They need coverage that doesn’t depend on luck or bandwidth. RingCX includes native AI Quality Management that automates QA scoring and compliance monitoring across 100% of contact center interactions, with no manual sampling required. Every call gets scored against your criteria automatically, and the output feeds directly into coaching workflows instead of sitting in a separate reporting tool. RingCX delivers on-the-spot AI coaching suggestions and helps leaders develop personalized coaching plans for their team. AI Quality Management also focuses on the customer side. Built-in customer intelligence automatically surfaces valuable insights and trends, including customer sentiment, common objections (and how agents handle them), competitor mentions, and reappearing keywords and topics. This helps you spot opportunities and adjust your scripts and coaching plans. If you’re evaluating your current QA stack against what full coverage actually requires, RingCX is worth comparing to your requirements list. Move from spot-checked monitoring to full coverage Coverage is what separates modern call center monitoring tools from legacy spot checks, not automation for its own sake. A platform that scores every call catches compliance drift on day one and gives supervisors coaching data based on patterns, not whichever calls got sampled that week. The math backs this up: under 5% manual coverage leaves the other 95% of your risk exposure invisible, while automated QA can cut review costs by more than half and lift agent efficiency by up to 30%. If your current QA process still depends on sampling, see how RingCX’s AI Quality Management scores every interaction instead of a fraction of them. FAQs about call monitoring software What is call monitoring software? Call monitoring software is a QA tool that automatically scores live and recorded calls against quality and compliance criteria, producing three outputs: a quality score, a compliance flag, and a coaching insight. It differs from traditional call recording, which only captures and stores audio and still requires a person to listen before any evaluation happens. How is call monitoring software different from call recording? Call recording produces an audio file, while call monitoring software produces an assessment of that file. Recording answers “what was said” and requires manual review to be useful. Monitoring answers “how well the call met your standards,” applying scoring criteria automatically across every interaction so no agent call goes unreviewed for lack of QA staff time. Can call monitoring software cover 100% of calls instead of a sample? Yes. Platforms built with native AI scoring, like RingCX’s AI Quality Management , evaluate every interaction automatically instead of relying on a manually sampled subset. That’s a structural difference from tools that still depend on a supervisor listening to a handful of calls each week. Does call monitoring software help with compliance, not just quality scoring? Yes. Automated monitoring flags procedural and regulatory gaps, like missed disclosures or skipped verification steps, at the moment they happen rather than during a retroactive audit. That shortens the window between a compliance miss and a corrective fix. Originally published Jul 27, 2026

title: Equinix Appoints Two Leaders to Executive Team
summary: Chris Audie joins company as Chief Product Officer Bruce Owen appointed Executive Vice President, Global Markets REDWOOD CITY, Calif., July 27,…...
body_text: Chris Audie joins company as Chief Product Officer Bruce Owen appointed Executive Vice President, Global Markets REDWOOD CITY, Calif. , July 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Equinix, Inc. (Nasdaq: EQIX), the world's digital infrastructure company®, today announced two senior leadership appointments reflecting the company's continued focus on accelerating product innovation and driving growth across global markets. Chris Audie will join Equinix as Chief Product Officer, responsible for leading the company's global products and services organization across interconnection, infrastructure, network operations, and ecosystem partnerships. Bruce Owen has been appointed Executive Vice President, Global Markets. A 16-year Equinix veteran, Owen will oversee the company's regional operations in the Americas, Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA), and Asia-Pacific. Both Audie and Owen report to Equinix CEO and President Adaire Fox-Martin. Innovating for Customers Audie brings deep experience spanning enterprise software, infrastructure automation and AI at some of the industry's largest technology companies. He previously served as HashiCorp's Chief Product and Technology Officer for Infrastructure and AI, leading product, engineering, and design. HashiCorp was acquired by IBM in 2025. "Chris is an engineer at heart who knows how to solve complex technical challenges at the intersection of infrastructure, software, and AI," said Fox-Martin. "Throughout his career, his technical depth, combined with his customer-centricity, have led to differentiated solutions at enterprise scale. Chris will be a tremendous addition to our team as we build the next generation of Equinix products and services that enable enterprises to simplify, connect, and manage an increasingly complex and distributed technology ecosystem." Prior to IBM and HashiCorp, Audie led product management for Generative AI and cloud platform capabilities at Google Cloud. He also held senior leadership roles at SAP, including SVP of Product Management and Partnerships for SAP's cloud platform. "The best product canvas in tech sits on physical infrastructure, and none is more interconnected than Equinix's, where the world's clouds, networks, and enterprises already meet," said Audie. "As AI continues to reshape how companies build and scale technology, the value of the infrastructure underpinning modern enterprises will only grow. Equinix's platform has been compounding for over two decades, and the demands of AI workloads make it more valuable than ever." Driving Global Growth Throughout his Equinix career, Owen has established himself as one of the company's most respected leaders, with a diverse mix of experiences spanning corporate development, finance, business operations, and regional leadership across the U.S. and Europe. Most recently, he served as President, EMEA. "Bruce is one of the most accomplished leaders we have at Equinix," said Fox-Martin. "His breadth of experience gives him a rare combination of strategic depth and operational credibility. I have great confidence in his ability to drive growth and bring our global markets together in ways that create real value for our customers." Before leading the EMEA region, Owen served as Managing Director for the United Kingdom, Equinix's largest EMEA market. He has also served as Chief of Staff to the CEO, as VP of Business Operations, and in other senior roles in the company's Finance and People teams. In addition, he previously held the position of President of the Equinix Foundation. "Across 36 countries around the world, Equinix goes where our customers want to place their most trusted workloads," said Owen. "Our regions pair global reach with local expertise, giving enterprises the confidence to deploy wherever they operate. I look forward to directing capital to the markets our customers need and building on our longstanding relationships with governments and communities." About Equinix Equinix, Inc. (Nasdaq: EQIX) shortens the path to boundless connectivity anywhere in the world. Its digital infrastructure, data center footprint and interconnected ecosystems empower innovations that enhance our work, life and planet. Equinix connects economies, countries, organizations and communities, delivering seamless digital experiences and cutting-edge AI—quickly, efficiently and everywhere. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from expectations discussed in such forward-looking statements. Factors that might cause such differences include, but are not limited to, risks to our business and operating results related to the current inflationary environment; foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations; stock price fluctuations; increased costs to procure power and the general volatility in the global energy market; the challenges of building and operating IBX® and xScale® data centers, including those related to sourcing suitable power and land, and any supply chain constraints or increased costs of supplies; the challenges of developing, deploying and delivering Equinix products and solutions; unanticipated costs or difficulties relating to the integration of companies we have acquired or will acquire into Equinix; a failure to receive significant revenues from customers in recently built out or acquired data centers; failure to complete any financing arrangements contemplated from time to time; competition from existing and new competitors; the ability to generate sufficient cash flow or otherwise obtain funds to repay new or outstanding indebtedness; the loss or decline in business from our key customers; risks related to our taxation as a REIT; risks related to regulatory inquiries or litigation; and other risks described from time to time in Equinix filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. In particular, see recent and upcoming Equinix quarterly and annual reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, copies of which are available upon request from Equinix. title: Slide Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: - Gross Premiums Written Grew 16.7% Year-over-Year to $508.0 Million - - Net Income Increased 92.4% Year-over-Year to $134.9 Million; $1.06 Diluted Earnings Per Share - - Combined Ratio Improved to 57.6% - TAMPA, Fla., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc.
body_text: Slide Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results July 28, 2026 PDF Version - Gross Premiums Written Grew 16.7% Year-over-Year to $508.0 Million - - Net Income Increased 92.4% Year-over-Year to $134.9 Million; $1.06 Diluted Earnings Per Share - - Combined Ratio Improved to 57.6% - TAMPA, Fla., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLDE) today reported results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Gross premiums written grew 16.7% to $508.0 million, compared to $435.4 million in the prior-year period. Total revenue increased 47.9% to $386.8 million, compared to $261.6 million in the prior-year period. Net income increased 92.4% to $134.9 million, compared to $70.1 million in the prior-year period. Diluted earnings per share for the second quarter of 2026 was $1.06. Combined ratio of 57.6% improved 980 basis points, compared to 67.4% in the prior-year period, reflecting lower loss ratio and improved operating leverage. Average return on equity in the quarter was 11.7%. “Our second quarter results reflect the continued strength of our operating model and disciplined execution,” said Bruce Lucas, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Slide. “We delivered another quarter of profitable growth while maintaining the underwriting discipline that has been central to our success. The scalability of our platform and our ability to capitalize on attractive opportunities position us well to execute our diversified growth strategy and create long-term value for our shareholders.” Second Quarter 2026 Operating Results Gross premiums written were $508.0 million, a 16.7% increase compared to $435.4 million in the prior-year period, driven by growth of voluntary new business and renewals of previously acquired Citizens policies. Net premiums earned grew 47.9% to $360.6 million, compared to $243.9 million in the prior-year period, while total revenue of $386.8 million increased 47.9% compared to $261.6 million in the prior-year period. The increase and year-over-year growth were directly driven by earnings growth from previous increase in voluntary homeowners and Citizens acquired policies. Losses and loss adjustment expenses (LAE) incurred, net were $108.7 million, compared to $91.4 million in the prior-year period. Loss ratio improved to 30.2%, compared to 37.4% in the prior-year period, primarily due to an improvement in overall loss experience. Policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses were $42.3 million, compared to $32.1 million in the prior-year period. The increase was driven by increased renewal policies from prior year assumed Citizens' policies, resulting in increased policy acquisition costs in 2026. General and administrative expenses were $55.0 million, compared to $37.9 million in the prior-year period, due primarily to the increased staffing costs and technology to support the Company’s strategic growth initiatives. The combined ratio improved to 57.6%, compared to 67.4% in the prior-year period, due primarily to improved loss experience and scaling impact in net earned premium growth with more moderate operating expense growth. Net income grew 92.4% to $134.9 million, compared to $70.1 million in the prior-year period. Diluted earnings per share for the second quarter of 2026 was $1.06 and return on equity was 11.7% in the quarter. Capital Allocation During the quarter, the company repurchased 2,997,980 shares of its common stock at a weighted average price of $17.95 per share. There remains $114.1 million of availability under the Company’s stock repurchase program. In addition, on July 27, 2026, the Company announced that it has declared an initial quarterly cash dividend of $0.07 per share on the Company’s issued and outstanding shares of common stock. The initial quarterly dividend will be payable on August 28, 2026, to stockholders of record as of August 14, 2026. Full Year 2026 Outlook The Company reiterated its expectations to generate gross written premiums in the range of $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion. Top-line growth is expected to be driven primarily by sustained organic expansion, including double-digit increases outside of Florida, complemented by selective growth opportunities within Florida that meet the Company’s return threshold. The Company also reiterated its expectations to generate full year net income in the range of $455 million to $470 million. Key Ratios In this press release we discuss certain key ratios, described below, which provide useful information about our business and the operational factors underlying our financial performance. Loss ratio , expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of losses and loss adjustment expenses incurred, net to net premiums earned. Policy acquisition expense ratio , expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of policy acquisition expenses and other underwriting expenses to net premiums earned. Expense ratio , expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of policy acquisition and other underwriting expenses, general and administrative expenses, and other operating expense to net premiums earned. Combined ratio is the sum of the loss ratio and the expense ratio. A combined ratio under 100% indicates an underwriting profit. A combined ratio over 100% indicates an underwriting loss. Return on equity , represents net income as a percentage of average beginning and ending shareholders’ equity during the period. title: Chances of Finding a Lost Cat After 24 Hours
summary: Enjoy and learn from Life360's blog archive, focused on user life stories and experiences with our premier family safety app.
body_text: Summary What this article covers: A clear look at the real chances of finding a lost cat after 24 hours, why most cats stay closer to home than you'd think, and the search steps that actually bring cats home faster. Who it’s for Pet parents whose cat has been missing for a few hours and the panic is starting to set in Indoor cat parents whose escape artist finally pulled it off Outdoor cat parents whose usually-on-time wanderer hasn't come back Anyone who wants a real answer instead of internet doom-scrolling at 2 a.m. Pet parents who want to be ready before their cat goes missing Key Takeaways The chances of finding a lost cat after 24 hours are actually pretty good. Indoor cats behave very differently from outdoor access cats when they go missing, and the search strategy should match. A thorough physical search of your immediate area in the first week is the single most effective way to find your cat. Posters, social media, and calls to local shelters and local vets all help, but they don't replace boots-on-the-ground searching. GPS trackers built for pets give you a head start most cat parents wish they'd had. If you've been pacing the house, shaking a treat bag, peering under the deck with a flashlight, and refreshing your front door camera every six minutes, first, deep breath. You are not alone, and this is not hopeless. The internet loves to scare cat parents into thinking that if you don't find your cat in the first 12 hours, all is lost. That's just not true. The chances of finding a lost cat after 24 hours are far better than the panic spiral wants you to believe. Cats are sneaky, weird little creatures with very predictable habits when they go missing, and once you understand those habits, the search gets a lot less scary. Here's what the research actually says, where most cats are really hiding, and what to do right now to bring your cat home. Your cat. Your map. No more pit-in-your-stomach moments. Life360 Pet GPS sends an instant alert the moment your cat leaves a familiar area — before the panic even has a chance to set in. See Life360 plans Why Most Cats Don't Go Far Cats are not little dogs. When a dog gets out, the dog runs. When a cat gets out, the cat hides. This is the silence factor, and it's why so many cat parents miss their cat the first time they walk past them. When cats go missing , especially indoor cats, they're not running for the horizon. They're frozen in place, tucked under a bush, holding very still, and absolutely not meowing back when you call. They're scared. The world outside got real big, real fast. Cats remember familiar territory and have a strong sense of where home is, but a startled cat trusts hiding more than running. Most cats will hide for about 24 hours if they are scared, and once the adrenaline and fear have worn off, they typically come out of hiding. That's actually great news for you. It means your cat is probably nearby, just waiting out the panic. Your job in those first 24 to 48 hours is to be where they can find you when they finally peek out. Indoor Cats vs Outdoor Access Cats Not all cats search the same. The biggest factor in finding a lost cat is honestly understanding which kind of cat you have. Indoor cats are the most common runaways and the easiest to find once you stop looking far away. An indoor cat that slipped out the front door is overwhelmed within minutes. They go silent, they freeze, and they pick the first dark, tight spot they can find. Think under your own porch. The neighbor's basement window well. The bushes against the side of the house. A garage someone left cracked. An engine compartment of a parked car. Outdoor access cats are different. They have a routine, they have a territory, and when they don't come home on schedule, something usually gets in the way. They might be stuck somewhere or chased off course by other animals or loud noises like fireworks or a passing dog. Outdoor cats run wider, but they also have better instincts to come back. They just may need a little time and an open door. If you're trying to find your cat, this distinction matters more than almost anything else. An indoor cat parent who searches three blocks over is wasting time their cat doesn't have. An outdoor cat parent who only checks their own yard is too narrow. What To Do in the First 24 Hours Act fast, but act smart. Here's a real-world order of operations. 1. Start with a thorough check inside your house. This sounds silly when you're convinced your cat is gone. Do it anyway. Cats are world-class hiders, and a surprising number of missing cat panics end with the cat asleep behind a dryer or wedged into a closet shelf you forgot existed. Open every closet, look behind every appliance, check every box. Most cats that disappear are never left. 2. Search your immediate area on foot. Walk slowly around your yard and the surrounding area. Look low under decks, in shrubs, inside open garages, near foundation gaps. Bring a flashlight, even in daylight; cat eyes catch the beam. Call your cat's name in your normal voice, then stop and listen. A scared cat won't yell back, but you might hear a tiny chirp. Then expand. Knock on neighbors' doors and ask permission to check their yards, sheds, and under their porches. Highly curious cats are more likely to be found inside someone else's house, so do not skip this step. The neighbor's basement is a real and frequent finding spot. 3. Search again at night. This is the move most pet owners forget. When the world is quiet, your cat is more likely to come out of hiding. Go out around dusk and again late at night. Bring a flashlight, a treat bag, and your cat's favorite squeaky toy or food bag. Call gently. Pause and listen. Repeat. 4. Set up a come home zone. Place your cat's litter box, a worn t-shirt of yours, and some cat food just outside your door (or near the suspected escape point). The familiar scent of kitty litter and home is one of the few signals that cuts through a cat's fear response and helps guide them back. 5. Tell the neighborhood, but smart. Post online your local Nextdoor, neighborhood Facebook groups, and any pet-finding apps active in your area. A clear photo, a contact number, and the cross streets near where your cat was last seen. Print missing cat posters and hang them at eye level near intersections, mailboxes, and bus stops. Good cat posters are simple: big photo, big MISSING CAT, cross streets, and your number. 6. Call local shelters and local vets. Call every shelter within at least a 10-mile radius, plus local vets. Give a clear description of your cat, matching what's on your poster. Ask them to check intake logs daily and follow up every few days. People who find a friendly cat often bring it to a vet to scan for a microchip first. When Should You Start Worrying More Seriously? If your cat has been missing for more than 48 to 72 hours and your physical search has come up empty, expand your radius and your effort. The first week is the most important window. Cats return home most often within that first week, but the cats that don't are usually trapped, injured, or have wandered into someone else's house. Keep posting online, keep calling local shelters and local vets every few days, and consider reaching out to a pet detective in your area. They aren't cheap, but they have search dogs, traps, and wildlife cameras that can find a cat that's gone too quiet for a regular search. And don't give up. Cats have been found alive after weeks, sometimes months. Cats return home in their own time, especially if they remember where home is. Don't hope. Know. Life360 Pet GPS puts your cat's real-time location on your family map — so the next escape ends with you walking toward a dot, not wandering in the dark. See Life360 plans How to Make the Next Disappearance a Lot Less Scary Here's the honest take: a GPS tracker built for pets won't stop your cat from getting out, but it will absolutely change what happens next. GPS collars and pet GPS trackers tap into satellite and cellular networks to show your cat's location on a map in real time. Instead of standing in your driveway shaking a treat bag, you're walking toward a moving dot. That's the difference between hoping and knowing. Life360 Pet GPS was built for exactly this moment. It puts your cat on the same map as the rest of your family, sends instant alerts if your cat leaves a familiar area, and includes built-in pet finding tools to help bring them home faster. Your cat, your people, and your favorite stuff all in one app, on one map. No juggling between apps when seconds matter. The cat parents who never want to feel that where are they?! pit in their stomach again are the ones who make the move before they need it. Your Cat Is Probably Closer Than You Think The chances of finding a lost cat after 24 hours are real, and they're better than the panic in your chest is telling you. So check the house. Check the yard. Knock on doors. Hang posters. Call the local shelters and local vets. Search again at night. Trust that your cat is closer than you think. And once your cat is home safely curled up on your lap pretending none of this ever happened, you'll probably want a way to make sure the next great escape ends a lot quicker. That's what Life360 Pet GPS is built for. Pets are family, too, and they belong on the same map as the rest of yours. Learn more about Life360 Pet GPS and bring everyone home faster.

title: How AI Video Upscaler Technology Is Transforming Video Production
summary: Discover how AI video upscaler technology improves quality, restores detail, and transforms modern video production.
body_text: Create AI videos with interactive avatars. Get started for FREE → Play an old video file next to a modern 4K screen and the quality gap is obvious immediately. For marketing teams, L&D departments, and creators, that gap forces a real decision: reshoot the footage or upgrade what already exists. Over the past few years, AI video upscaler tools have become the practical answer for the second option. Key Takeaways An AI video upscaler improves the resolution of existing footage by predicting plausible detail, not by simply stretching the image. Video upscaling AI works especially well for archive footage, training content, and social videos that need to hold up on modern screens. A YouTube AI upscaler can bring older uploads up to a more competitive quality level. The workflow is typically simple: upload the video, choose a target resolution, and wait for rendering. Upscaling improves visual quality, but it cannot rescue footage that is weak in content or badly damaged to begin with. What an AI Video Upscaler Actually Does Traditional upscaling fills in missing pixels by averaging the values of neighboring pixels. The result usually looks soft and blurry, because no real new image information is added. Video upscaling AI works differently. The model is trained on large sets of video pairs and learns what detail was likely present in the original before it was compressed or shot at a lower resolution. It adds edges, texture, and sharpness where they are statistically likely to belong, rather than blending pixels together. In practice, that looks like this: a blurry face gets sharper edges. Compression artifacts, the blocky patterns typical of heavily compressed video, get smoothed out. Backgrounds with flat, noisy grain start to look cleaner. What an AI video upscaler does not do is invent content that was never there. A whiteboard filmed over someone’s shoulder with illegible handwriting will usually still be illegible, just with cleaner edges around it. The source footage sets a hard ceiling on the result. Why Video Upscaling Matters for Modern Content The bar for acceptable video quality is noticeably higher today than it was five years ago. YouTube’s recommendation systems favor higher-resolution content. Phones and laptops now ship with high-density displays as standard. And a corporate screencast played on a 27-inch monitor makes low resolution obvious within seconds. Anyone managing a library of older marketing videos, training material, or webinar recordings faces the same question: reshoot or upgrade? For content that is factually outdated, reshooting is the only real option. For footage where the message still holds up, upscaling is the faster and cheaper path. Common quality problems and what AI upscaling does about them: Quality issue before upscaling Result after AI upscaling Pixelated, blocky image (720p or lower) Sharper image in HD or 4K Visible compression artifacts Reduced artifacts, cleaner edges Unclear facial detail Recognizable facial features Soft text rendering (captions, graphics) Crisper edges on text and overlays Grainy or noisy footage Noticeably reduced noise For a closer look at how AI editing keeps existing footage usable for longer, see the piece on AI video repurposing . Common Use Cases for AI Video Upscaling Making archive footage usable again. Companies that have been recording product videos, webinars, or trade show sessions for years often end up with large archives sitting at 480p or 720p. Dropping that footage straight into a current campaign looks dated. Upscaling brings the image quality up to a modern standard without a reshoot. Preparing content for YouTube and social media. A youtube ai upscaler helps creators and brands improve older uploads, or publish new content at a consistently high resolution. On platforms where image quality is a direct signal of production value, upscaling is often the difference between a video someone watches and one they scroll past. Refreshing training videos and internal communications. L&D teams frequently work with older training material that is still accurate but visually out of step with current brand standards. Instead of reshooting every course, upscaling can lift the visual quality of what already exists. The same logic applies to video marketing on LinkedIn, where visual consistency matters just as much, as covered in the piece on upscaling LinkedIn video marketing . Adapting video for different screen formats. Digital signage, presentation displays, and modern conference room screens often run at a higher native resolution than the source file. Upscaling reduces the visible quality drop when that footage plays on larger or sharper hardware. For brands running AI-generated content across multiple channels, this also comes up in AI video influencer marketing , where image quality needs to hold up consistently across every output channel. How to AI Upscale a Video in a Simple Workflow The process looks similar across most AI video upscaler tools: Prepare the source file. Start with the best available version of the footage, ideally without extra compression added before upload. Choose a target resolution. Most tools offer 1080p and 4K as output options. A realistic step is something like 720p to 1080p. Jumping from 360p straight to 4K rarely produces a convincing result. Check a preview. Many providers offer a short preview of a few seconds before committing to the full render. This saves time if the result does not meet expectations. Start the render and wait. Cloud-based tools typically take between 5 and 30 minutes for a 3 to 5 minute video, depending on server load. Locally run software often takes considerably longer, depending on hardware. Check the result on the target device. The upscaled video should be tested on the actual output format, not just in a browser preview window. The time investment is modest. Cloud-based tools require no technical infrastructure, which makes them workable for teams without a dedicated post-production department. Choosing the Right AI Video Upscaling Tool No video upscaling tool performs equally well in every scenario. Anyone planning to ai upscale video regularly as part of their workflow should evaluate a few things first: Output quality on your own source material. The only reliable test is uploading a real sample file and judging the result directly. Vendor demos are usually tuned to flatter their own model. Processing speed and batch capacity. Anyone upgrading an entire video library needs a tool built for bulk processing. Uploading files one at a time for hundreds of videos is not a workable option. Data privacy and storage. Corporate videos containing internal content should only go through platforms where it is clear where files are processed and how long they are retained. Export formats and compatibility. The upscaled file needs to fit the target format, whether that is YouTube, an LMS, or an internal presentation deck. For teams that also want to produce new video directly in high resolution, AI video generators offer a complementary option. D-ID’s Video Studio, for example, creates presenter-style videos with AI avatars directly at up to 1080p, with no camera or post-production required. That is a different approach from upscaling, but it addresses the same underlying need: quality video content without a traditional production process. Yes, within limits. AI video upscaling noticeably improves sharpness and reduces compression artifacts on archive footage. On very poor source material, below 360p or heavily compressed files, results stay limited. The cleaner the original file, the better the upscaling outcome tends to be. Yes. A YouTube AI upscaler can lift older uploads to 1080p or 4K, which improves perceived quality. Higher resolution does not replace weak content, though. Platform algorithms weigh engagement more heavily than resolution alone when deciding what to promote. With cloud-based tools, a 3 to 5 minute video typically takes 5 to 30 minutes, depending on server capacity, target resolution, and file format. Software running locally usually takes considerably longer, depending on the hardware available. Generally, yes. Result quality depends on the source footage and content, not on video length. Longer videos simply mean longer render times and larger file sizes. Some tools also cap maximum video length on lower-tier plans. Start with the best available version of the source file, without extra compression added before upload. It also helps to confirm the target format and platform in advance, so the tool can select the right output resolution and codec for the job.

title: The Vanishing Findings: What Happens When You Apply Real Statistics
summary: The market knowledge your talent decisions depend on — centralized. Verata unifies company intelligence, executive data, and search management in one platform built for PE talent and executive search.
body_text: The vanishing findings have a direct operational implication: most of what you have been told about what makes a successful PE CEO is statistically unsupported. This is not a claim about any specific study or consultant. It is a mathematical consequence of how the research has been conducted. For your firm, the action items are specific and implementable. Apply skepticism to CEO trait claims. When a search firm, consultant, or internal team asserts that a given trait predicts CEO success, ask for the evidence. Specifically, ask whether the finding survived correction for multiple comparisons and whether it replicated across independent samples. If the answer is no -- or if the question has never been asked -- the claim is unvalidated. Demand replication, not novelty. The valuable finding is not the new trait that emerges from the latest study. It is the trait that has replicated across multiple studies with proper correction. In our data, only two traits clear this bar. Recognize the asymmetry. Your competitors are making CEO selection decisions based on the full, uncorrected set of 'findings.' If you make decisions based on only the validated subset, you are operating with a cleaner signal. This is a structural advantage. Build internal evidence. Track your own hires against your own outcomes. Over time, you will accumulate a proprietary dataset that lets you distinguish signal from noise within your specific portfolio context. The drug trial analogy is not hyperbole. You are making a decision that will affect hundreds of millions of dollars in enterprise value. The question is whether you want to base that decision on evidence that would survive FDA review or evidence that would not.
